dedupe_keys.name: thames estuary 2100 adaptive flood risk plan and its monitoring reviews

description: Thames Estuary 2100 is the Environment Agency's adaptive plan for managing tidal flood risk in London and the Thames Estuary to the end of the century, reviewed on a fixed monitoring cycle. It covers the estuary from Teddington to the Isle of Grain and Shoeburyness across 27 local councils, with phases to maintain defences to 2035, upgrade them and decide the end-of-century option for the Thames Barrier by 2040, and implement it by 2070; indicators are reviewed every 5 years and the plan every 10 years. The 15-year monitoring review of August 2026 found relative sea level rise of 4.1 mm per year from 1993 to 2024, now matching the plan's projection, 96.4 per cent of fixed defences at required condition, 211 barrier closures from 1982 to 2025, and 1.51 million people and 743,000 homes within the plan area. The plan was published by the Environment Agency and partners in 2012 and updated in 2023. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): OGL-UK-3.0. Access is free of charge. Caveats: tidal forecasting is not yet meeting its accuracy target. It informs adaptive planning for flood defences protecting multi-sector infrastructure; a related record is the European coastal exposure and vulnerability dataset.
